core_obligations: Record that the statement makes sense and derive representability of the maps from the stages from the representability of the diagonal (proof lines 2064-2068).

For a morphism from a scheme into the space, use the Zariski local factorisation through a later stage to express the fibre product with the stage under consideration as a fibre product over that later stage (proof lines 2068-2076).
Conclude that the projection of that fibre product to the test scheme is a base change of a thickening, hence a thickening (proof lines 2076-2077).
proof_roadmap: Local factorisation and the base change computation (proof lines 2068-2077).
difficulty_reason: For a presentation of an affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the lemma asserts that each stage maps to the space by a representable thickening (statement lines 2056-2062). The proof first records that the statement makes sense, and then obtains representability of the maps from the stages from the earlier result on the diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 2064-2068). For the thickening property it tests against a morphism from a scheme: the discussion following the definition of an affine formal algebraic space shows that Zariski locally on the test scheme the morphism factors through some later stage, and on such a piece the fibre product with the stage under consideration is the fibre product over that later stage, hence a base change of the thickening between two stages (proof lines 2068-2077). The claim is H2: representability is taken from a named result, and the thickening property is verified by a local factorisation and a base change computation, both displayed.
